allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Every year, thousands of Antarctica's emperor penguins make an astonishing journey to breed their young. They walk, marching day and night in single file 70 miles into the darkest, driest and coldest continent on Earth.  This amazing, true-life tale is touched with humour and alive with thrills. Breathtaking photography captures the transcendent beauty and staggering drama of devoted parent penguins who, in the fierce polar winter, take turns guarding their egg and trekking to the ocean in search of food. Predators hunt them, storms lash them. But the safety of their adorable chicks makes it all worthwhile. So follow the leader... to adventure!!

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: As storms rage and predators circle, the parents must trade duties across frozen miles—leaving the fragile egg's survival hanging on precise timing.
visibleEditorialCopy.description: In Antarctica, thousands of emperor penguins march seventy miles across ice and bitter winter winds to breed, trading off ocean treks and egg protection to keep their offspring alive.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Deliberate and visually sweeping, balancing polar survival tension with accessible, family-friendly warmth.
